answer:
I've completed the research. Here's a summary of the key findings for forecasting whether **Marquita Bradshaw** wins the Aug 6, 2026 TN Democratic Senate primary:

**Bottom line:** Bradshaw is the presumptive front-runner **by name recognition only**, but the field is wide open with no polling and no prediction markets.

**Points favoring Bradshaw:**
- Only candidate to have won a statewide Democratic primary (2020, 35.2% in a 5-way race)
- Former nominee with ~1M general-election votes and highest name ID
- Memphis base (large Black Democratic electorate); TN has no runoff, so a plurality wins
- Field is fragmented (5 candidates), which can help a recognizable name

**Points against Bradshaw:**
- Lost the 2024 primary badly (24.4% vs. Gloria Johnson's 70.6%)
- Anemic 2026 fundraising — FEC shows only **~$2,257** in cycle receipts
- Outdated/weak campaign operation; no major endorsements
- Maria Brewer (ex-party staffer) is running the most polished operation; Miller-Watkins has strong local roots (though got only 1.8% in 2024)

**Notable clarifications:** This is a **regular** election vs. incumbent Bill Hagerty (not a special election), Tennessee is Safe Republican, and **no polling or prediction market data exists** for this race. All findings are current as of late July 2026, pre-primary.

key_facts: The Aug 6, 2026 TN Democratic Senate primary has 5 candidates: Marquita Bradshaw, Maria Brewer, Kevin Lee McCants, Civil Miller-Watkins, Diana Onyejiaka — winner faces GOP incumbent Sen. Bill Hagerty.
It is a regular election (Hagerty seeking 2nd term), NOT a special election; TN rated Solid/Safe Republican; Democrats haven't won a TN Senate seat since 1990.
Bradshaw is the only candidate to have previously won a statewide Democratic primary — she won the 2020 Senate primary with 35.2% and got 1,036,858 votes (35.1%) in the 2020 general.
Bradshaw LOST the 2024 Senate primary decisively, getting 24.4% (50,094 votes) vs. Gloria Johnson's 70.6%.
Bradshaw's 2026 fundraising is minimal: FEC committee C00846048 shows only ~$2,257 total receipts for the cycle; reporting calls it 'only a few thousand dollars.'
No candidate has any major political/institutional endorsements; Bradshaw's listed endorsements are only informal 'Sway' voting-group picks.
Civil Miller-Watkins ran in the 2024 Senate primary and received only 1.8%.
Kevin Lee McCants is running simultaneously for both U.S. Senate and Governor in 2026.
Diana Onyejiaka had no functioning campaign website as of mid-July 2026 and is the least publicly defined candidate; she entered but withdrew from the 2020 race.
Maria Brewer is a former Tennessee Democratic Party staffer running a polished but low-budget campaign.
No polling and no prediction markets (Polymarket/Kalshi) exist for this primary; press outlets explicitly decline to name a frontrunner.
Tennessee has no primary runoff, so a plurality wins — Bradshaw won 2020 with ~35% in a similar 5-way field.
Early voting ran July 17–Aug. 1, 2026; a strong-start report noted ~75,000 early ballots cast statewide.
